parts.text: A student is determining the spring constant k of a spring by two methods. Fig. 1.2 shows how the apparatus is used. Method 1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 1.1, measure the unstretched length l 0 of the spring, in mm. Fig. 1.1 l 0 = ................................................. mm [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student attaches the spring to the clamp as shown in Fig. 1.2. He hangs a 300 g mass on the spring. Fig. 1.2 He measures the new length l of the spring. 53 l = ...................................................... mm

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the extension e of the spring using the equation e = l – l 0 . e = ................................................. mm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value for the spring constant k using the equation k = F e , where F = 3.0 N. k = ............................................ N / mm [1] Method 2

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student pulls the mass down a short distance and releases it so that it oscillates up and down. Fig. 1.3 shows the time t taken for 10 complete oscillations. Fig. 1.3

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record the time t taken for 10 complete oscillations. t = ........................................................ [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the spring constant k using the equation k = 0.040 m T 2 , where m = 0.300 kg. k = ............................................ N / mm [1]
